- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes — if price spiked recently, forecast should be capped or smoothed to avoid lagged overcorrection.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is significantly above or below recent 18d average, reduce magnitude of deviation toward historical mean.
- Forecast horizon 30d often lags true outcome by 1–3 days; if sentiment is volatile, add 1–2 day lag correction to align with sentiment momentum.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with cycle phase — adjust forecast to match sentiment phase (e.g., bearish sentiment → lower forecast).
